qualifications: Ten focused configurations each passed all 13 normal streaming decoder tests: safe, unsafe-byte-cursor, unsafe-bitstream, unsafe-ring-history, unsafe-fse, unsafe-huffman, unsafe-dictionary, all features, and no-default-features safe/all. The eight std configurations list the single live oracle as ignored in the ordinary suite; both release oracle invocations separately passed it.

Seven new normal tests cover zero-payload construction and fresh owner identities, reset and changed window-cap ownership, all nine prepared fixtures over four fragment schedules with reset replay, independent shared/borrowed dictionary domains, every observed allocation request on four representative decode workloads, a small four-request failure sweep, prefix claim/reset/drop and skippable handling, and resource validation before allocation.

Four targeted strict-provenance all-feature Miri checks passed: constructor/reset/window owner changes; small allocation-failure recovery sweep; shared custom dictionary lifetime; prefix/skippable/error lifetime. Full fixture and failure campaigns ran natively across all ten configurations, not entirely under Miri.

Existing sequence_encoding, upstream_decodecorpus, upstream_dictionary and upstream_streaming integration suites passed both safe/all: 93 normal tests with four explicitly ignored external/oracle tests in each run. No additional ignored tests are claimed as run.

Live oracle used the existing pinned v1.5.7 executable outside the repository. Each safe/all release invocation compressed eight checksum frames with/without a formatted dictionary and decoded all eight through both borrowed/shared custom allocator contexts, 16 decodes per invocation. This is C-to-Rust decoder interoperability, not C byte-identical compression or a benchmark.

Prepared dictionary table payloads are never copied per frame. Borrowed views keep original lifetimes; Global Arc/Rc control ownership remains an explicit exception around custom-allocated dictionary payloads.
Process errors retain poisoning-until-reset and provisional-output semantics. Retained capacity includes reachable attached dictionary payloads once, excluding inline and Arc/Rc control storage.
The context retains an allocator factory A; ordinary cloning may follow caller panic/allocation policy, but existing payloads never move between different allocator instances.
Parent/sibling source updates changed filtered-out totals during verification; selected normal decoder counts remained 13.
The checked compiler is nightly-2026-10-08 reporting 1.101.0-nightly. No unavailable Rust 1.100 execution is claimed.
